title: Kirchhoff's second law and conservation of energy practice

question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use prior learning: q01 directly retrieves Lesson 4 and q07 mixes the current loop law with current conservation.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: prior retrieval, conceptual diagnostics, direct loop balance, signed source reasoning, then mixed current and energy conservation

evidence_basis.originality_note: All contexts, wording, values and figure briefs are original; mapped evidence grounds only the assessed definition and loop-law demand.

questions.prompt: State Kirchhoff's first law and name the conservation principle that explains it.
Which statement is Kirchhoff's second law?

options.A: The current entering every component equals the current leaving it.
options.B: The sum of e.m.f.s equals the sum of potential differences around a closed circuit loop.
options.C: The resistance around any loop is zero.
options.D: Every component in a loop has the same potential difference.

questions.prompt: Why does the algebraic sum of potential changes around a closed loop equal zero?

options.A: Charge returns to its starting point with no net change in energy per unit charge.
options.B: Current is used up before reaching the source.
options.C: Every resistor supplies energy to charge.
options.D: A source has no internal resistance.
